_about: Hellenistic and late Greek poets in English, translator per title, all raw IA OCR with title pages read: Callimachus (William Dodd, 1755 per the catalogue), Aratus (John Lamb, 1848; Edward Poste, 1880; Robert Brown Jr., 1885), Tryphiodorus (James Merrick, 1739), Oppian's Halieutica (Oxford, 1722; translators attributed) and Musaeus (Edwin Arnold). Mair's 1921 and 1928 Loebs (Callimachus, Lycophron, Aratus; Oppian, Colluthus, Tryphiodorus) are Greek facing and held back like the other Greek-facing Loebs.

callimachus-dodd-hymns: The Hymns of Callimachus, translated from the Greek into English verse, with select epigrams and the Coma Berenices (London; 1755 per the catalogue, the imprint date is lost in the OCR)
aratus-lamb-phenomena: The Phenomena and Diosemeia of Aratus, translated into English verse (London, Parker, 1848)
aratus-poste-skies: The Skies and Weather-Forecasts of Aratus (London, Macmillan, 1880)
aratus-brown-phainomena: The Phainomena, or Heavenly Displays, of Aratus, done into English verse (1885)
tryphiodorus-merrick-destruction-of-troy: The Destruction of Troy, being the sequel of the Iliad, translated from the Greek of Tryphiodorus (Oxford, 1739)
musaeus-arnold-hero-leander: Hero and Leander, from the Greek of Musaeus (Cassell, Petter and Galpin)
oppian-diaper-jones-halieuticks: Oppian's Halieuticks, of the Nature of Fishes and Fishing of the Ancients, in V Books (Oxford, 1722)
tr. William Diaper and John Jones (attributed; the title page names no translator)
